name: Beth Chen

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I am a senior researcher with the Work Futures Panel. We are independent of employers, AI firms, unions and government, and your answers are confidential. What does a usual workday involve?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I am 43, have a bachelor’s degree in accounting and am still a junior learning how to draft returns at this firm. I prepare small-business accounts and ask our senior reviewer to correct the tax codes I miss. I sometimes use an approved AI lookup after colleagues have tried it, but I check each result against the client’s receipt. I like helping a small-business owner understand a figure, but late missing receipts make the end of the day tiring.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What does home look like when you leave?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: Rowan, my partner, works evening hospital shifts, so I collect our two school-age children and make dinner. Our mortgage is manageable on my well-paid junior job and Rowan’s wage, and we have around eight months of expenses saved. There are plenty of accounting firms nearby, but I prefer a move only after seeing the paid hours and pickup plan.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say small software savings are all right when we still check a client’s tax return. I would rather use the extra minutes to get a missing invoice than hurry through the sign-off.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our mortgage and school costs are manageable because I am paid well for this junior role and we have about eight months saved. A little automation does not make me fear for my income, but I still need to learn the tricky returns.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I would keep preparing small-business accounts and use the approved AI lookup I sometimes use only after my senior reviewer has checked the source. In the first year I would keep my current client files and put 50 a month of actual pay into our emergency account while both wages hold.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel calm about the household, with the usual worry about making a mistake. I would not call a quicker lookup a new career.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: When did the lookup help?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A client sent a box of receipts from a flower stall, and the lookup grouped dates for me. I checked each receipt against the bank statement before I gave the file to my senior.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What makes the emergency account useful?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: It paid the car repair last spring without touching the mortgage money. I want to replace that withdrawal before we spend more on family outings.

say: I would use small **software savings** to chase missing invoices.
I would still check **tax returns** before sign-off.
think: Our **eight-month cushion** and high junior pay keep us secure here.
I still need help with **tricky returns**, regardless of faster lookup.
do: Keep preparing **small-business accounts** with approved lookup and senior source checks.
Deposit **50 monthly** from current pay into emergency savings while both wages hold.
feel: I feel **calm** about income while staying careful with client figures.
S0.quote: I would not call a quicker lookup a new career.
fieldNote: Her **flower-stall file** shows occasional AI use under senior review, with every receipt checked against the bank.
The **50 monthly deposit** is genuinely new savings from pay, meant to replace cash used for a car repair.

steps.text: Keep preparing small-business accounts with approved lookup and senior source checks
Deposit 50 monthly from current pay while both wages hold

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the owner that junior staff need paid time to learn what the software misses. A client should still know which accountant asked for the missing invoice.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Booking figures and drafting simple tax notes are a lot of my day, so the firm might cut some of my hours. Eight months saved and many nearby firms give us room to respond, though I would rather keep this job while learning.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I would ask my senior reviewer to let me test the approved draft tool on four closed flower-stall returns during paid hours, recording the mistakes. In the first year, if my hours are cut, I would apply to advertised local junior tax posts only with written salary and hours at least equal to now, keeping my current shifts until a written offer and start date.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about possible lost hours, but the mortgage is covered for a while. A test on old files is a sensible way to learn without using a live client as practice.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you ask for a new title?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No, I want a supervisor who can correct me on real work. A nicer title without a paid training hour would not make me better at the job.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does family time fit the test?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The test has to happen during paid office hours because Rowan, my partner, is on evening hospital shifts and I collect our children. I would not promise unpaid evenings to prove I can use a tool.

say: I would ask for **paid junior learning** when software takes simple work.
I would keep a **named accountant** responsible for missing-invoice questions.
think: My **booking and tax-note hours** could shrink as software handles more first drafts.
Eight months saved and **many nearby firms** give us options.
do: Test **four closed returns** on the approved tool during paid hours with senior review.
After lost hours, apply to **advertised local junior posts** with written equal pay and hours, keeping shifts until offer and start date.
feel: I feel **anxious** about possible lost shifts while the mortgage remains covered.
S1.quote: A nicer title without a paid training hour would not make me better at the job.
fieldNote: Her **tool test** is limited to closed files under senior review and paid hours because she handles evening childcare.
She will keep **current shifts** until a local vacancy has written equivalent terms and an actual start date.

steps.text: Test four closed tax returns with approved tool during paid hours and senior review
Apply to advertised junior posts after cuts with written equal pay/hours; keep shifts until start date

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say AGI by 2028 reaches tax desks in 2028, before capable robots arrive around 2031. The firm should give junior staff a written forecast rather than wait for the rota to vanish.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect the first drafts and invoice booking I do to shrink sharply when cheaper thinking work arrives. Eight months of savings helps, but a new junior post may pay less even if several local firms advertise.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I would ask the owner for written notice of any hour cut and stop planning the expensive family holiday, keeping the unpaid travel money in our account. If my hours fall in the first year after 2028, I would apply for a vacant paid client-records intake post at this firm only with written salary and hours at least equal to mine; if there is none, I would apply to advertised local junior posts while keeping paid shifts until a confirmed start date.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about losing our higher wage, though we can search for months. I would not assume intake calls are safe forever just because people still want to speak with someone.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the intake post involve?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ring clients for missing receipts and explain what papers the senior accountant needs. I would still need a supervisor to check my advice, and a paid rota that fits school pickup.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if no firm offers the same pay?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would use some of the eight-month reserve to search longer while keeping any paid account shifts. I would only accept less after Rowan and I look at the mortgage numbers together.

say: I would say **AGI by 2028** reaches our tax desk before capable robots.
think: My **first drafts** and invoice booking may shrink sharply in 2028.
Our **eight-month reserve** gives time, but equal pay may be scarce.
do: Stop planning the **expensive holiday** and retain unspent travel money.
After cuts, seek a **vacant paid intake post** with written equal salary, hours and school-pickup rota under senior supervision.
If none opens, apply to **advertised local posts** while employed; consider lower pay only after reviewing the mortgage with Rowan.
feel: I feel **anxious** about replacing high pay despite a strong reserve.
S2.quote: I would not assume intake calls are safe forever just because people still want to speak with someone.
fieldNote: She sees **2028 desk exposure** clearly and does not present client phone work as immune from cheaper AGI.
The **intake move** needs supervision, written equivalent pay and a school-compatible rota; she will use savings before accepting a lower wage.

steps.text: Cancel expensive holiday plan and retain unpaid travel money
Seek vacant paid intake post after cuts with written equal pay/hours, school-compatible rota and supervision
Apply to advertised local posts while keeping shifts until confirmed start date if no intake vacancy
Review mortgage numbers with Rowan before accepting lower-paid local offer after cuts

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the firm AGI by 2031 gives us five years to train people for the client work that remains paid. Robots arriving around 2034 are later than the change to tax screens.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Five years lets me practise speaking with clients and build another cushion, though I expect simple drafting to shrink in 2031. I would want the senior reviewer checking my advice before I take calls alone.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I would ask the owner to fund a short course in client records and give me paid supervised intake calls twice a month. If fees and paid hours are approved in writing, I would enrol next year; I would save 110 monthly while both wages hold, and in the first year after 2031, if my draft hours fall, I would take a vacant paid intake role only with written salary and hours at least equal to now and a school-pickup rota, or keep current shifts while applying locally.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious, with time to gain practice. I still need a real paid post, not just a course completion letter.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the owner will not pay for the course?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask my senior reviewer to let me practise two old intake calls during paid office time if she agrees. I would not use our emergency savings for tuition.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What happens if the intake vacancy is on evenings?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would decline unless Rowan confirms an actual hospital shift swap and the children have a safe pickup. I would not put a hopeful swap on the family calendar.

say: I would ask for **paid supervised intake** before 2031.
I would note **2034 robots** do not postpone tax desk changes.
think: My **simple drafting** still faces a 2031 reduction in paid hours.
I need **supervisor checks** before handling client calls alone.
do: Enrol in a **client-records course** with written fees, paid hours and supervised calls; otherwise practise old calls if senior agrees.
Save **110 monthly** while both wages hold.
After cuts, take **vacant paid intake** only with written equal pay/hours, confirmed hospital swap and safe pickup; otherwise apply locally while employed.
feel: I feel **anxious**, with time to practise before changing roles.
S3.quote: I would not put a hopeful swap on the family calendar.
fieldNote: Her **course plan** requires written funding and paid hours, with supervised old calls as the free fallback.
An **evening intake shift** is acceptable only after Rowan confirms a hospital swap and the children have safe pickup.

steps.text: Enrol with written fees and paid hours; otherwise practise old calls with senior during paid time
Save 110 monthly while both household wages hold
Take vacant intake after cuts with written equal pay/hours, confirmed Rowan swap and safe pickup
Apply locally while keeping paid shifts if no suitable intake vacancy opens

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say AGI by 2036 gives the firm time to keep a proper paid path for juniors and families time to save. Capable robots around 2039 do not delay the tax desk change.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our children will be older and the mortgage smaller if our wages stay steady. I still expect basic return drafting to go in 2036, but I could have spent years learning client records work by then.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I would keep preparing returns and ask for one paid supervised client intake shift a month if the manager agrees. I would hold twelve months of household expenses in cash, then pay an extra 160 monthly against mortgage principal while both wages hold; in the first year after 2036, if draft hours fall, I would take a vacant paid intake role only with written salary and hours no worse than today and a confirmed family pickup plan, or apply to advertised local posts before leaving.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel calm about the next few years, with money and time to learn. I would still count actual paid intake shifts rather than assume every client wants a person in 2036.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you buy a new qualification now?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only if an employer names a real paid role and funds the fees and paid study hours in writing. I would not take household cash from the mortgage reserve for a hopeful certificate.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell the children about work?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say learning from a patient person matters even when a machine can finish the form. I want the children to see work as service, not just faster paperwork.

I would remind colleagues the **tax desk** changes before hands-on robots arrive.
think: Basic **drafting work** may end when AGI reaches our tax screens in 2036.
The **mortgage balance** can fall if both wages continue.

S4.quote: I would still count actual paid intake shifts rather than assume every client wants a person in 2036.
fieldNote: Her **long runway** plan counts actual paid client work and protects a twelve-month reserve before extra mortgage payments.

steps.text: Learn intake on paid supervised monthly shifts only if manager agrees

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because my drafts could shrink before I learn enough client work to replace the pay. A written staffing plan, supervised paid calls and a real vacancy would help.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask who collects the children when an office job moves to evenings. A paid offer without a pickup plan is only half an offer.

headlineQuote: A paid offer without a pickup plan is only half an offer.
portrait: At **43**, Beth is a junior accountant with a bachelor’s degree, still learning small-business accounts and tax codes.
She and **partner Rowan** have two school-age children, a mortgage, high junior pay and eight months saved.
She uses **AI occasionally** after colleagues test it and can consider many nearby firms.
The **2028 scenario** threatens her drafts; longer runways let her practise paid client intake with a confirmed childcare plan.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could reduce her draft hours before a comparable paid intake role opens.
whatWouldHelp: She wants **written staffing plans**, supervised paid calls and a real vacancy that fits school pickup.
